item.title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

item.title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.31727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

item.title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism, a moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting, has so far been realized primarily in N\'{e}el-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron-chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g., $\uparrow \uparrow \downarrow \downarrow$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[C_2||{\cal T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and finite inter-chain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the K$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_4$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice $C_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

item.title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer B$_{x}$Al$_{1-x}$N and B$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B$_{0.25}$Ga$_{0.75}$N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V$_2$O$_5$ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6$\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$. A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.

item.title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
item.description: arXiv:2610.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

item.title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.

item.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

item.title: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) under finite electric displacement fields: a removable $\alpha\!\to\!\delta$ reorientation barrier and a persistent first-order $\delta\!\to\!\beta$ conformational change
item.description: arXiv:2610.31926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $\alpha$, $\delta$, and $\beta$ phases of PVDF are interconverted by electrical poling and mechanical drawing, yet the thermodynamics under a controlled electrical boundary condition has not been established from first principles. We evaluate the zero-temperature free energy at fixed electric displacement $D$ from van der Waals density-functional calculations along two constrained coordinates in a common 24-atom cell: a tilt of the gauche C--C bonds that maps antipolar $\alpha$ onto polar $\delta$ (cell change $<1\%$), and a backbone torsion that straightens TG$^+$TG$^-$ chains into all-trans $\beta$ (chain-repeat strain $10.6\%$). As $D$ increases from 0 to $0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, the lowest homogeneous free energy switches from $\alpha$ to $\delta$ at $D_{c1}=0.046$~C\,m$^{-2}$ and from $\delta$ to $\beta$ at $D_{c2}=0.157$~C\,m$^{-2}$. At $T=0$ with domain-wall energy neglected, a $\delta$ multidomain state lies $14.3$~meV per cell below homogeneous $\alpha$ at every $D$. A $\Gamma$-point harmonic estimate suggests that vibrations reverse this ordering at room temperature. $\delta$ and $\beta$ coexist for $0.11<D<0.21$~C\,m$^{-2}$ at $E^*=0.69$~GV\,m$^{-1}$, independent of the screening constant. The tilt barrier falls from $0.66$~eV per cell at $D=0$ to $17$~meV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$ (below $k_BT$ at $300$~K), while the torsion barrier remains $0.66$~eV at $D_{c2}$ and $0.34$~eV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, so $\delta\to\beta$ stays first order. Much of the difference traces to the path effective charge ($0.28e$ for the tilt, $0.18e$ for the torsion). Scaling shows the tilt barrier would survive with the torsion charge; the smaller torsion charge accounts for about half the barrier it retains. The landscape accounts for why a field produces $\delta$ and why $\beta$ is reached by drawing, and suggests that raising that charge could let a field alone produce $\beta$.

item.title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
item.description: arXiv:2610.31934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840{\deg} C and 925{\deg} C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. Structural analysis of the latter sample revealed a high density of strain-relieving interfacial dislocations, identified primarily as Lomer-type or 60{\deg}-type, that accommodated the ~4% lattice mismatch between the two materials, while chemical analysis showed very limited interfacial intermixing. Crystallographic analysis showed that the interface faceting was associated with rutile {101} facets, with characteristic facet angles of ~114{\deg}; these observations support thermally driven TiO2 (001) substrate faceting rather than an interface reconstruction resulting from GeO2 epitaxy. Overall, these findings provide useful insights into the mechanisms governing interface formation and strain relaxation in r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructures and suggest that further refinement of growth conditions should enable improved epitaxial growth of r-GeO2 for future ultrawide-bandgap electronic device applications.

item.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
item.description: arXiv:2610.31976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monoclinic $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

item.title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
item.description: arXiv:2610.32228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.

item.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic ${\alpha}$-MnTe
item.description: arXiv:2610.32261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor ${\alpha}$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of ${\alpha}$-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to ${\alpha}$-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated $E_{2g}$ phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in ${\alpha}$-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in ${\alpha}$-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.

item.title: Flexo-Photoresponses from First Principles
item.description: arXiv:2610.32341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. Applying the framework to prototypical centrosymmetric materials, including Si, cubic $\rm SrTiO_3$, and monolayer black phosphorus, we demonstrate that a strain gradients of $10^5\sim10^6~\rm m^{-1}$ can induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects comparable to the intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for strain gradient engineering of light-matter interactions, opening new avenues for nanoscale optomechanics, optoelectronics, and beyond.

item.title: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Otto, Leon Brauns, Benjamin Schroeder, Claus Ropers

item.title: On the Role of Atomic Mobility in the Polyamorphism of Metallic Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.32434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms underlying polyamorphic transitions requires simultaneous knowledge of thermodynamic and structural evolution, which has remained experimentally inaccessible. Here, we combine chip-based fast differential scanning calorimetry with high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction to simultaneously probe the thermodynamic and structural evolution during the polyamorphic transition of a Pd-Ni-P metallic glass. Correlating heat-flow signals with the corresponding structural evolution during both heating and cooling reveals a direct relationship between thermodynamic evolution and medium-range structural ordering. Based on this relationship, we identify two distinct transition mechanisms. In the glassy state, the transition proceeds continuously through progressive medium-range ordering, accompanied by enhanced thermal stability and strongly temperature-dependent kinetics. In contrast, in the equilibrium supercooled liquid, the transition proceeds through the coexistence of distinct amorphous states, with only a weak temperature dependence of the kinetics. These findings show that atomic mobility governs the transformation pathway by coupling thermodynamic evolution to structural ordering, providing new insights into polyamorphic transitions in nonequilibrium amorphous systems.

item.title: Side-Chain Engineering Controls Molecular Packing and Vertical Electron Transport in Discrete n-Type NDI-T2 Oligomers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.

item.title: Divalent Yb in the Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ Structure Type: Crystal Growth and Physical Properties of Yb$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the single-crystal growth, crystal structure, and physical properties of Yb$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$. Single crystal x-ray diffraction shows that the material crystallizes in the Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ structure-type at ambient conditions, described by orthorhombic symmetry $Pbam$. Magnetization measurements reveal a nearly isotropic diamagnetic response, indicating that Yb is stabilized in a non-magnetic divalent configuration. Electrical resistivity measurements show a metallic behavior. First-principles calculations including spin--orbit coupling describe a metal whose states at the Fermi level are dominated by Bi $6p$ orbitals, with a density of states within 1% of that of the isoelectronic compound Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$, consistent with a filled and chemically inert $4f$ shell. They further show that the nonsymmorphic symmetry of the crystal enforces fourfold-degenerate nodal lines on the Brillouin-zone boundary, four of which cross the Fermi level and give symmetry-enforced Dirac points with a linear transverse dispersion. Despite strong metallic and covalent bonding within the Pd-Bi network, Yb$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ is realized as a rare-earth analog of the Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ structure type with divalent Yb ions. This result offers a potential avenue to discover other rare-earth analogs within this structural family.

item.title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
item.description: arXiv:2610.32553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10 nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al$_2$O$_3$-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0 s (untreated), 20 s, 40 s, and 60 s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (1.24-6.20 eV) and infrared (0.041-0.827 eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9 eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60 s reduced the effective carrier concentration from $1.20 \times 10^{22}$ to $1.03 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-3}$ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.

item.title: High-quality, deep formation and identification of oxygen-vacancy defects in silicon carbide
item.description: arXiv:2610.32642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optically addressable paramagnetic defects in silicon carbide (SiC) are attractive for scalable quantum technologies such as quantum sensing. PL5, PL6, and PL7 are promising defects for their high brightness and spin-readout contrast. Although generation by oxygen implantation has been reported very recently, nonuniform spin and optical properties and the limited generation depth of implanted defects hinder both high-sensitivity sensing and conclusive microscopic identification. Here we engineer high-quality defects by decoupling oxygen incorporation and defect formation, realizing highly homogeneous spin-resonance frequencies as well as narrow optical linewidths and long T2* coherence time. Further, we demonstrate defect formation beyond the ion range utilizing oxygen diffusion, exceptional among impurities in SiC. We further provide hyperfine-interaction statistics of 17O and host nuclei across many PL6 defects, making the oxygen-vacancy origin conclusive. Together, the microscopic identification and the demonstrated formation route establish a foundation for developing the oxygen-vacancy spin defect into a versatile quantum platform.

item.title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.32678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal materials are designed either by screening known crystals for a target property or by generating new crystals with that property. Both routes are judged against public databases of known crystals, but these databases name the same crystal differently. Several materials announced as new by recent generative and autonomous discovery campaigns have since proved to be known phases or close variants of them. The limits of both routes remain unmeasured. Here we probe them by matching the crystals of 55 databases by structure into one self-extending database of 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values, each traced to its source. Only 4.5% of its crystal-property pairs carry a value. To fill the empty pairs, we developed CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer with state-of-the-art accuracy on several tasks of two public benchmarks. Trained on each task, it forms a library of property models whose predictions we release. The reach of forward screening has been underestimated. Known crystals hold tens of thousands of ultra-incompressible candidates without a recorded bulk modulus, and a post hoc audit of synthesis evidence finds among them ReN2, whose bulk modulus was measured at 428 GPa. The novelty claimed for inverse design has been overestimated. At an equal verification budget, a stiffness-conditioned generator returned more stiff hits than screening (100 versus 55), but all contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions. Integrating and completing the databases of known crystals therefore moves the limits of both routes: it widens what screening can reach and sets the reference against which generated crystals are judged new.

item.title: On the Spontaneous Structural Reconstructions of Chalcogen-Depleted MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, and Janus MoSSe Monolayers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Removing one chalcogen layer from a transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayer leaves an undercoordinated sheet that reconstructs as the remaining chalcogen atoms cross the metal plane. Here, we combine \textit{ab initio} and reactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of depleted MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, and Janus MoSSe, examining each remaining chalcogen on two parent lattices, to show that the remaining chalcogen type determines the structural reconstruction, with only a minor influence from the parent lattice. In \textit{ab initio} trajectories of the Janus-derived sheets, Se crosses the Mo plane already at 300~K, whereas S stays in place at 300~K and the sheet reconstructs only at 900~K. With a free in-plane cell, the crossings precede an anisotropic lattice contraction, which therefore results from the structural reconstruction. Reactive MD simulations of 50~nm sheets show that, when S remains, the Mo lattice stays crystalline in nanometric domains that disappear with time and temperature, with pores/holes at 900~K. In contrast, when Se remains, the Mo lattice loses crystalline order within the first picosecond, and 36--39\% of the Se atoms cross at every temperature. In a depleted lateral MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterostructure, both modes coexist in one sheet, each half reconstructing like its single-chalcogen counterpart, suggesting chalcogen patterning as a route to define crystalline and disordered regions in a single monolayer.

item.title: Controlled Fabrication of Uniform Columnar Porous GaN Architectures by Electrochemical Etching
item.description: arXiv:2610.32722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrochemical etching (ECE) of n-type c-plane GaN enables the formation of porous architectures capable of enhancing the performance of optoelectronic devices and broadening the range of possible GaN applications. Here, we demonstrate that the addition of NaOH to Na2C2O4 (and other non-acidic etchant solutions) directs ECE toward the formation of nanoscale, vertically aligned, highly uniform columnar pore morphologies with relatively limited surface roughening. By varying the NaOH concentration within mixed electrolyte systems, the columnar pore shape, diameter, spacing, and bulk and surface porosity can be readily tuned. In addition to manually mixing NaOH with another etchant, aqueous basic electrolytes such as Na2CO3 and Na3PO4, each inherently containing significant hydroxide concentration through hydrolysis, also produce similar columnar pore morphologies, indicating that hydroxide plays the key role in directing the vertical pore growth. Chronoamperometry and pore structure analysis reveals that the mixed hydroxide-containing electrolyte systems exhibit a distinct, new ECE mechanism rather than a simple superposition of the individual ECE behaviour of each anion present. This work provides significant insight into the ECE mechanism for porous GaN, which is proposed to contain multiple reaction steps where hydroxide anions are involved in the formation of a reactive intermediate. These findings establish a versatile and controllable route for engineering columnar porous GaN architectures, offering significant advancement in applications requiring high porosity, ordered, and bespoke structures.

item.title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
item.description: arXiv:2610.32791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length $\lambda_\sigma$ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem). Structural order heals over a distinct mechanically-dressed length $\xi_G$; their ratio $\kappa_G=\lambda_\sigma/\xi_G$ provides the structural counterpart of the Ginzburg-Landau parameter. Because the matrix is transiently rigid yet locally relaxational only over an intermediate time window, the same mechanism selects crystal for slow protocols, a heterogeneous G state at intermediate rates, and a homogeneous L-like glass under rapid arrest. Residual incompatibility frustrates coarsening, allowing finite ordered cores and screened, orientation-dependent core interactions. The resulting texture is an inverted Abrikosov analogue: structural order resides in the cores, whereas incompatible-stress screening is carried by the surrounding disordered matrix. The theory yields direct simulation and experimental tests through stress-decay, structural-healing, non-affine-susceptibility, and kinetic measurements.

item.title: Rationalizing charge transfer: a single-molecule case study across three distinct surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.32903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.

item.title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

item.title: CO2-Induced Shifts in the Confined Phase Transformation of CH4 in Metal-Organic Frameworks
item.description: arXiv:2610.32918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sharp increase in gas uptake over a narrow pressure range can occur for fluids confined in nanoporous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), reflecting a transformation between distinct adsorption states, often accompanied by the existence of metastable states. Understanding how co-adsorbed species modify this behavior is important for predicting and optimizing gas storage and separation. Here, we investigate the effect of CO2 on the adsorption transformation of confined CH4 in rigid IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8. Transition-Matrix Monte Carlo (TMMC) simulations were performed for systems containing 0-75 and 0-150 CO2 molecules in IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8, respectively. While the addition of CO2 decreases the maximum CH4 uptake, consistent with competition for pore space, remarkably, the presence of CO2 significantly shifts the discontinuity in the CH4 adsorption isotherm to substantially lower pressures relative to the pure CH4 system. This promotion of the high-density CH4 phase at lower pressures demonstrates that CO2 substantially alters the thermodynamic landscape governing confined CH4 through changes in both fluid-fluid and fluid-framework interactions. These results establish CO2 as a thermodynamic modifier of confined CH4 behavior and suggest that controlled co-adsorption provides a means of tuning adsorption transformations in nanoporous materials.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Dorhauer, Bartosz Mazur, Bogdan Kuchta, Carlos Wexler

item.title: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
item.description: arXiv:2610.32938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sluggish vacancy-mediated self-diffusion in lithium metal limits the critical current density (CCD) of Li anodes in solid-state batteries by promoting interfacial void formation during stripping. To enhance the effective vacancy concentration while preserving the bcc Li host, we screen 50 substitutional solutes using density functional theory (DFT) within a funnel based on automatic phase diagram construction, solution energies, solute-vacancy binding energies, and experimental solubility limits. Using an adaptation of the Lomer model for the dilute limit, we show that only Ag, Ge, and Cd solid solutions are predicted to reach $1~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ within their solubility limits. The thermodynamically estimated CCD of Ag at $\sim 9$ at.% reaches $\sim 4~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ at a theoretical capacity of $1522~\mathrm{mAh~g^{-1}}$. Migration barrier calculations indicate that the enhancement may be partially offset by vacancy trapping, necessitating further validation via molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, Hume-Rothery rules alone prove insufficient as prefilters, whereas machine-learning models trained on the DFT data can eliminate most unsuitable solutes early in the funnel and extend the workflow to related solid-solution searches.

item.title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
item.description: arXiv:2610.31805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single $s-p$ energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a {\it single} electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav M. Silkin, Maxim Yu. Kagan

item.title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
item.description: arXiv:2610.31952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.

item.title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.

item.title: Boundary shape controls the stress distribution in two-component elastic materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.32072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate how the shape and arrangement of high-stiffness regions govern stress redistribution in two-component triangular elastic spring networks subjected to spatially correlated and uncorrelated random prestress. We compare boundary roughness, partitioning into disconnected regions, and graded transitions between regions of different stiffness. Our simulations identify interface bonds as channels for energy transfer: increasing their number provides additional transfer paths and reduces stress concentration in mechanically rigid regimes, while offering little benefit in compliant subnetworks. This is analogous to defects in naturally occurring crystal structures, where the defects themselves isolate stress. At a fixed fraction of high-stiffness material, partitioning reduces stress concentration for both correlated and uncorrelated prestress. The benefit diminishes with further subdivision as the number of interface bonds becomes comparable to the number of interior nodes. Stress reduction, however, depends on the spatial correlations of the imposed prestress: random prestress generally yields a stronger effect, though the difference diminishes in some regimes. Graded interfaces further reduce peak stress by distributing the stiffness transition over a broader region. Together, these results suggest design strategies based on increasing interface area, matching subdivision scale to prestress correlations, and grading stiffness transitions. This minimal framework identifies how internal structure controls energy transfer and stress redistribution, suggesting design principles for mechanical robustness under both internal and external loading.
item.dc:creator: Kyungeun Kim, Adam Clare, Miranda Holmes-Cerfon

item.title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

item.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
item.description: arXiv:2610.32121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Shchepkin, D. V. Karlovets

item.title: Compass Correlations in a Square-Lattice Magnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.32157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er$^{3+}$ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-$Q$ vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.

item.title: Triplon dynamics from partial Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Nakahara, Masahito Mochizuki, Rintaro Eto

item.title: Strain-tunable van Hove singularity and superconducting dome in monolayer kagome metal CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain ($\varepsilon$) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature $T_C$ exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of $\varepsilon=+2\%$. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Run Lv, Wenqian Tu, Dingfu Shao, Yuping Sun, Wenjian Lu

item.title: Magnetic Anisotropy and Magnetization Dynamics in Si/Ni Multilayers Probed by FMR and VSM Magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.32565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The magnetic anisotropy and magnetization dynamics of sputtered [Si(40~\AA)/Ni($t_{\mathrm{Ni}}$~\AA)]$_{20}$ multilayers were systematically investigated at room temperature using SQUID--VSM magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance (FMR). Static measurements reveal soft ferromagnetic behaviour in thicker Ni layers and mixed ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions at reduced thicknesses. The saturation magnetization increases toward the bulk Ni value with increasing thickness, consistent with Ni nanocrystallite growth. Magnetic dead-layer analysis yields an interfacial dead-layer thickness of approximately $9$~\AA\ per interface, accounting for the suppressed magnetization in thinner Ni layers. Angle-dependent FMR measurements reveal effective easy-plane magnetic anisotropy, while out-of-plane spectra exhibit additional non-uniform spin-wave modes. The effective magnetization remains lower than the static saturation magnetization, indicating a perpendicular anisotropy contribution that partially compensates the demagnetizing field. Quantitative anisotropy analysis yields an interfacial anisotropy constant of $K_S = +0.17~\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}}$, favouring perpendicular magnetization, and a volume anisotropy constant of $K_V = -1.23 \times 10^6~\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-3}}$, favouring in-plane alignment, with an extrapolated anisotropy crossover thickness of $t_c \approx 27$~\AA. Increasing FMR line-shape asymmetry with decreasing Ni thickness is consistent with enhanced interfacial roughness. These findings highlight the competing interfacial and volume anisotropies and the importance of Ni thickness and interface quality in tailoring Si/Ni multilayers for silicon-compatible spintronic applications.
item.dc:creator: Dushyant Singh, Subha Maity, Tharundev V V, Subhavenkadesh SS, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte

item.title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the \bar{M} point in 2.4{\deg} twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.32714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the \bar{M} point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4{\deg} twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the \bar{K} point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Feraco, Przemys{\l}aw Przybysz, Oreste De Luca, Ying Wang, Pavel Dudin, Jos\'e Avila, Jianting Ye, Pawe{\l} D\k{a}browski, Pawe{\l} J. Kowalczyk, Jagoda S{\l}awi\'nska, Petra Rudolf, Antonija Grubi\v{s}i\'c-\v{C}abo

item.title: First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. When the system is translationally invariant in space or time (the latter case corresponding to an equilibrium condition), these two-point correlators reduce to one-variable functions of the remaining variable. Remarkably, these functions are both reminiscent of critical behaviour, including divergent correlation times and lengths signalling the phase transitions. Away from these conditions, namely in non-periodic systems or genuinely dynamical processes, criticality is instead better captured by higher-order Chern-Chern correlators constructed from local or dynamical markers obtained as coincident-point limits of the position correlators. These higher-order Chern-Chern correlators can be seen as double Levi-Civita contractions of second-order position correlators, selecting the antisymmetric sector in each index pair. We substantiate this framework through numerical simulations and analytic calculations. Our results establish a general correlator-based description of topological phase transitions, applicable to crystalline, noncrystalline, equilibrium, and dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Antimo Marrazzo, Christian Loer Llemit, Massimo Capone

item.title: Tensor Networks for Materials Simulation and Quantum Chemistry
item.description: arXiv:2610.32754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting the properties of correlated materials and molecules often requires a many-body description that goes beyond single-particle and mean-field approximations. Tensor networks address this challenge by exploiting the entanglement structure of quantum states to construct compact, systematically improvable representations. Although developed largely for idealized model Hamiltonians, these methods are increasingly being integrated into material-specific calculations. This Perspective introduces their underlying principles and examines how network geometry, bond-dimension truncation, and approximate contraction determine the accuracy and computational reach of these approaches. We survey applications across regimes of increasing complexity, ranging from ground-state properties of quantum magnets and itinerant-fermion systems to excitation spectra, nonequilibrium dynamics, finite-temperature and open systems, and molecular electronic structure. We then examine four routes connecting these methods to real materials, including experimentally constrained models, downfolded Hamiltonians, dynamical mean-field theory with tensor network impurity solvers, and quantum embedding. Throughout, we evaluate the maturity of existing capabilities and their principal limitations, synthesizing this assessment into a practical method-selection guide. We argue that reliable materials predictions require quantifying uncertainties introduced at each stage, from constructing material-specific Hamiltonians to extracting experimentally accessible observables. Finally, we identify the algorithmic advances and reproducible computational practices needed to establish tensor networks as a routine tool for predictive materials science and quantum chemistry.
item.dc:creator: Saeed S. Jahromi, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Roman Rausch, Sukhbinder Singh, Roman Orus

item.title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.32767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.

item.title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.32797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.

item.title: Intrinsic defects and 4d/5d transition metal defects in Cr$_2$O$_3$: pathways for enhancing the N\'eel temperature
item.description: arXiv:2506.10883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: First-principles calculations are employed to explore avenues to increase the N\'eel temperature ($T_{\mathrm{N}}$) of the magnetoelectric antiferromagnet Cr$_2$O$_3$ through doping. Employing the hybrid functional method, we calculate the formation energy of intrinsic defects and transition metal dopants (Mo, W, Nb, Ta, Zr, and Hf) to assess their likelihood of formation. Intrinsic defect calculations indicate that Cr interstitials and oxygen vacancies dominate under Cr-rich conditions, whereas Cr vacancies prevail under O-rich conditions. Notably, under Cr-rich conditions, the Fermi level can be pinned slightly above mid-gap due to the formation of Cr interstitials and oxygen vacancies. Additionally, we identify a split Cr vacancy configuration that is more energetically stable than a normal Cr vacancy in corundum Cr$_2$O$_3$. To assess the influence of dopants on $T_{\mathrm{N}}$ of Cr$_2$O$_3$, we calculate the enhancement of the exchange energy for the spin at the dopant site or at an adjacent Cr site using the supercell method.Our study identifies isovalent Mo and W substitutions at Cr sites as the most promising candidates for increasing the N\'eel temperature because of impurity-mediated enhancement of the exchange interaction for half-filled bands. Formation-energy calculations indicate that Mo and W substitutions at Cr sites form more readily under Cr-rich conditions and that a Fermi level near or slightly above midgap stabilizes the desirable neutral charge states of the Mo and W defects. This is assisted by the formation of intrinsic Cr interstitials and O vacancies under Cr-rich conditions. These findings offer a route to utilize defects for higher $T_{\mathrm{N}}$and enhanced performance of Cr$_2$O$_3$ in magnetoelectric devices and provide useful guidance for future experimental studies.

item.title: Laser Melting and Loss of Interlayer Coherence of the Charge Density Wave Order in TiSe${_2}$ observed by time-resolved neutron diffraction
item.description: arXiv:2509.15358v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-resolved elastic neutron scattering combined with laser-induced heating was used to probe the evolution of the periodic lattice distortion (PLD) associated with charge-density-wave (CDW) order in 1T-TiSe$_{2}$. Upon pulsed laser heating, the crystal undergoes a phase transition, where the transient response of the average lattice is isotropic. In contrast, the PLD exhibits an anisotropic behavior. The superlattice intensity is rapidly suppressed in-plane and out-of-plane upon heating, consistent with melting of the ordered state, but recovers more quickly in-plane than along the c-axis as the sample cools below the CDW transition temperature. The out-of-plane component shows pronounced broadening due to reduction of the interlayer correlation length while the in-plane correlations recover. The disparity between the nearly isotropic lattice response and the anisotropic recovery of the superlattice demonstrates that the CDW dynamics cannot be described solely by the evolution of the average lattice temperature. Instead, the results indicate that interlayer phase coherence represents the slowest-relaxing component of the ordered state. These findings support a picture in which the CDW instability is established primarily within the 1T-TiSe${_2}$ layers, while three-dimensional long-range order depends on weaker coupling between layers. More broadly, they demonstrate how direction-resolved time-resolved neutron diffraction can disentangle thermal and correlation-driven contributions to CDW dynamics in low-dimensional materials.

item.title: AtomMOF: All-Atom Flow Matching for MOF-Adsorbate Structure Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2602.07351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for applications such as direct air capture, where performance depends on how adsorbates bind within the framework. Accurately predicting MOF-adsorbate configurations is therefore important for screening candidate materials. However, traditional approaches are computationally expensive and require a known host structure, while existing generative models rely on rigid-body assumptions and do not explicitly model adsorbates. We introduce AtomMOF, a scalable all-atom flow-matching model that jointly predicts MOF-adsorbate structures from discrete building blocks and adsorbates. Built on a Diffusion Transformer with a building block-based pairwise attention bias, AtomMOF operates in an unconstrained all-atom space and exhibits clear scaling behavior. To improve the structural validity of flexible all-atom models, we also propose Feynman-Kac (FK) steering with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). On the BW dataset, AtomMOF achieves a 58.17% relative increase in match rate and a 31.84% relative reduction in RMSD compared with prior work. MLIP-guided steering further improves validity by 28.7% and reduces formation energy error by 86.5%. On ODAC25, AtomMOF generates adsorption configurations faster than GCMC and, when combined with MLIP relaxation, identifies lower-energy configurations than those in the reference dataset.

item.title: Revealing Charge Transfer in Defect-Engineered 4Hb-TaS2
item.description: arXiv:2603.24486v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of defects in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$. In this layered transition metal dichalcogenide, charge transfer between alternating Mott-insulating 1T and metallic 1H layers gives rise to exotic quantum phases such as the Kondo effect and topological superconductivity. Motivated by recent defect manipulation in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$ via STM, we address their microscopic nature and impact on interlayer charge transfer. To this end, we systematically analyze over 90 defects using large-scale density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Our analysis identifies 1H sulfur vacancies, Ta-on-S antisites, and Ta interstitials as the most likely origins of the commonly observed defects, with Ta-on-S antisites producing the strongest charge-transfer modulation. Our extensive dataset, compiled from STM simulations, defect formation energies, work functions, and charge transfer, establishes a foundational resource for future theoretical and experimental studies on defect engineering in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$.

item.title: Dilute Zn alloying in biodegradable Mg wires: microstructure, mechanical performance, and degradation behavior
item.description: arXiv:2605.00221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dilute Mg-Zn wires are of great interest for biodegradable small-bone fixation, as magnesium degradation can support bone-related processes, while low zinc additions may provide biological benefits without compromising biocompatibility. In this work, the influence of Zn content below the room-temperature solubility limit was assessed in Mg-Zn wires intended for resorbable implant applications. Mg-0.4Zn, Mg-0.6Zn, Mg-0.8Zn, and Mg-1.5Zn alloys were processed by single-step direct hot extrusion into thin wires and characterized by correlative microstructural analysis, tensile testing, bending experiments, and in vitro degradation. All compositions achieved a recrystallized fine equiaxed grain size of 5.0-5.9 um and exhibited ultimate tensile strengths of 246-256 MPa with elongations of 23-28 %. In these thin wires, Zn content had only a limited effect on grain size, tensile properties, and bending behavior, although lower-Zn alloys showed a pronounced sharp yield point. Bending was governed mainly by extrusion texture and preserved reversible plasticity through twinning and detwinning. Simulated body fluid caused rapid localized degradation and loss of mechanical integrity within 7 days, while the biologically more relevant DMEM-based medium better reflected the expected in vivo response. Together, these findings support dilute Mg-Zn wires as a simple material platform for the development of future resorbable bone fixation devices.

item.title: Limitations of Debye-Waller lattice temperature extraction under electronic excitation
item.description: arXiv:2605.15140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ultrafast diffraction is the cutting-edge technique to extract the atomic temperature at femtosecond timescales, and further related quantities - in particular, electron-phonon coupling strength at elevated electronic temperatures. The present work demonstrates limitations of such an analysis, emphasizing the importance of careful evaluation of the evolution of the Debye temperature. It is shown that, due to the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to this parameter, neglecting its changes under electronic excitation may lead to significant deviations of the atomic temperature extracted from its true values.

item.title: Machine Learning Assisted Design of Complex and High Entropy Alloys by Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD Process for Low Carbon Energy Applications in Extreme Environments
item.description: arXiv:2608.01903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Complex and high entropy alloys are attracting much attention currently thanks to their mechanical and corrosion resistance properties in harsh environments, in particular needed for carbon-free energy applications. However, their elaboration in bulk and in thin film form in a trial-and-error approach is impractical due to their complexity and the cocktail effect. The recent development of artificial intelligence brings a new possibility for their elaboration and adjustment of their properties. Firstly, we present an overview of Materials and data science research. Then we describe how DIADEM - French initiative for Materials and Data science convergence - tackles the development of innovative coatings for carbon-free energy applications (nuclear, high temperature electrolysis, ...) thanks to the development of a nationwide network of synthesis and characterization platforms - the DIADEM discovery hub. We describe in particular DIADEM-2D, an AI-driven Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD process using 4 cathodes in confocal combinatorial configuration. We present the high entropy alloy determination using data from the literature for corrosion resistance in molten salt media and nuclear accidental conditions. An element-independent model gathering deposition parameters and coating properties has been implemented allowing the design of protective coatings with a particular composition. We demonstrate the feasibility of this process and its accuracy.
